parts.text:
The design review overrides 7 points. I need to write 07_diag_revision.md with full M01-M13 updated actual-function/order/check matrix, incorporating the rulings.

Let me re-read the key files targeted (I already have them in context from the previous turn: calibrate_sensors.py, ground.py relevant, bag2session.py). The instruction says "Use targeted current source, not full history" and "Do not reread full files/history." I already have the source content. But to be safe about current SHA, let me recompute SHAs of the 3 key source files to confirm unchanged since my diag (07046..., 2d25..., e3c3...). And re-read the prompt/acceptance? I have them in context. The user says read them; I already read them last turn and they haven't changed. I'll re-verify SHAs and maybe quickly confirm acceptance unchanged. Read-only.

Actually the prompt is mostly the same. Let me just verify SHAs and re-read the acceptance quickly to ensure no changes. And the prompt. But "do not reread full files/history" — I'll rely on context but verify hashes.

Let me compute hashes of prompt, acceptance, PLAN_REVIEW, and the 3 sources, to confirm.

Then write 07_diag_revision.md.

Key rulings to fold in:

1. Explicit declaration entry: prepare only supports `--source-dir` (fixed meta.json+points.bin), `--frame required`, `--units required and only "m"`, `--output`. No default innolidar/m, no arbitrary `--meta/--bin/--groups` extension. meta.frame non-empty and matches declaration; if meta.units has explicit record, must match; unknown type rejected. Always metadata_declared/physical false.

2. Deterministic actual frame identity: one bundle one complete source. Fixed one group per frame, no caller partition/alias config. Group ID generated by deterministic formula from path-independent source meta/bin content identity + frame ordinal/seq/stamp; records member as that complete frame range. Loader rebuilds from actual source and checks formula + complete ordered members; changing group name/member cannot self-report pass. Independence only means disjoint source frame sets, not statistical/physical independence.

3. Actual source reconstruction three-way equality: loader reads actual meta/bin, rebuilds canonical source XYZ f4 bytes/frames/group; NPZ points must be exactly Nx3/little-endian f4, no object/extra columns/silent conversion; actual source XYZ digest == NPZ raw points bytes digest == manifest expected digest; source meta/bin SHA, layout, declared/unknown flags, frames/group each layer checked. Three self-consistent declared hashes not enough, cannot call hash anti-forgery. Missing source rejected.

4. All entries recognize manifest: shared input loader/main entry recognizes key. adapted only allowed constrained; non-constrained explicitly return 2 before any write, cannot ignore marker to go legacy. Corrupt NPZ with marker never fallback; normal points without key keep old behavior, cannot give adapted lineage qualification.

5. Preserve selector types, group-first: shared selection helper accepts original region selector + group. bounds first restrict to actual members, then coordinate bounds, map back to pooled original rows; out-of-group coordinates also not hit (not error). Explicit pooled indices must all be in declared group, cross-group rejected. fit and validation use same helper; forbid turning region first into indices over full pool and losing type. Missing fit selector/group/priors or fewer than 3 explicit validation → reject, no auto select. Existing ground funcs still check point/frame isolation, no math change.

Wait - "组外坐标也命中不属于错误" — let me parse: bounds first restrict actual members, then coordinate bounds; "组外坐标也命中不属于错误" means coordinates outside group also matched is not an error? Hmm. Actually reading: "bounds先限制实际成员，再做坐标bounds，映回pooled原行；组外坐标也命中不属于错误。" I think it means: after restricting to actual members, apply coordinate bounds; [the fact that] out-of-group coordinates would also be hit [by the bounds] is not an error — because we already limited to group. i.e., no error raised for coordinate overlap; group-first makes it irrelevant. Let me phrase: group-first ensures only group members are considered; coordinates that would match outside the group don't count and don't trigger an error.

6. adapted single output & order: first version adapted rejects `--diagnostics` (explicit error before write); full diagnostics still readable in `artifact.constrained_ground`, old normal points diagnostics semantics unchanged. All source/selection/fit/export/derived/reference_axis/full artifact validation before first write; adapted invalid fit and missing export conditions return 2 with no artifact. Success emits only one immutable calibration JSON; no claim two-path transactional atomicity.

7. Atomic exclusive: new NPZ only uses same-dir complete temp + flush/fsync + os.link exclusive publish; lacking this ability → explicit reject, no fallback to direct O_EXCL copy exposing half target. adapted calibration also reuses existing save_exclusive_json only when atomic exclusive link supported (old legacy fallback unchanged), pre-validate full JSON then single output. Construct/input/algorithm reject before write; target competition existing file preserved. temp cleanup only own temp files.

Also: initial M09 "cross-pool bounds both pass and reject" and M11 O_EXCL fallback not retained. Initial run_constrained only probes manifest, prepare missing declarations/custom groups no canonical, old invalid first writes diag facts all verified. Write new 07_diag_revision.md mapping rulings per M01-M13 to actual new functions/old entry order and tests, stop at READY_FOR_DESIGN_REVIEW.

So the revision must:
- prepare CLI: only --source-dir, --frame, --units, --output. No --groups. Groups deterministic one-per-frame.
- Group ID deterministic formula. Need to define a concrete formula. E.g., group_id for frame i = "frame_" + hashlib.sha256(canonical_source_identity + b"|" + str(ordinal) + "|" + str(seq) + "|" + str(stamp_sec) + "|" + str(stamp_nanosec)).hexdigest()[:16]. Or path-independent source identity = bin_sha256 (content). Since bin_sha256 is path-independent content identity. And meta content. So group_id = "g" + sha256(bin_sha256 + f"{ordinal}:{seq}:{stamp_sec}:{stamp_nanosec}").hexdigest()[:16]. Member = [[ordinal, ordinal]] i.e., single frame. The loader recomputes and checks.

- No caller partition/alias. So M08 "same source frame different group name" becomes: there is exactly one group per frame; a caller cannot name groups, CLI selection uses region.frame_group but must equal the deterministic group id for the selected frame(s). For validation regions, each region must be within a single frame's group? Hmm. The ground fit requires fit_frame_group string and each region frame_group string, all distinct. With one-group-per-frame, the region must select points from exactly one frame (its group). fit may also be one frame. Then independence = distinct frames. If a caller tries to label two regions with the same frame's group id, duplicate group → rejected. If caller tries to create arbitrary group names, they won't match deterministic formula → reject.

Actually "固定每帧一个group，无caller分区/alias配置；group ID由...确定性公式生成，记录成员为该完整frame range". So the manifest has n_frames groups, each group = one frame. Callers reference group ids (must be valid manifest ids). The gate maps each region to its group's actual frame ordinal via the deterministic id, and verifies selected indices belong to that frame's rows. Fit group likewise.

But wait — can fit span multiple frames? With one group per frame, no: fit_frame_group is a single frame group. So fit selection is restricted to one frame. That's the deterministic design. Validation each one frame, distinct frames, >=3. That's fine and matches "先限制实际group成员".

Hmm, but is that too restrictive? The review says "固定每帧一个group" — yes, fixed one group per frame. So fit and each validation each correspond to one frame. Independence = disjoint frames. OK.

- Selector type preservation: shared helper `select_group_region(context, region)` takes the raw region dict (with either `indices` or x/y/z bounds) + its `frame_group`, and:
  - resolve group to actual frame ordinal (must be a manifest group id).
  - restrict to member rows of that frame: candidate = indices of that frame's rows.
  - if region has `indices`: these are pooled rows; each must be in group member set; return np.unique sorted intersection? Actually explicit pooled indices must all be in group, cross-group rejected. So check all in set, then return normalized unique.
  - if bounds: apply coordinate bounds to the member subset only; return pooled rows (original indices) that satisfy.
  - return pooled original row indices.
- fit uses same helper with fit_frame_group.
- Missing fit selector/group/priors or <3 validation → reject.

- Ground still called with fit_indices and regions (list of dicts with region_id/frame_group/indices as pooled). ground will re-check overlap/leakage. But ground's region frame_group strings are the deterministic group ids; distinct frames → distinct ids. Good. No math change.

- artifact.constrained_ground holds diagnostics; adapted rejects --diagnostics.

Now "All entries recognize manifest": not just run_constrained. The shared input loader `load_input` (used by both legacy main and run_constrained) must detect manifest. Ruling: "在shared input加载/主入口识别含key。adapted只允许constrained；非constrained在任何写入前明确return2". So `load_points` or `load_input` detects. Design: add detection at the top of `main`/`load_input`. Since legacy `main` (non-constrained) also calls `load_input`, if adapted marker found and not constrained → return 2 before any write. And `run_constrained` allows. Corrupt marker → reject in both.

Concretely: `capture_input.classify(path)` returns "legacy" | "adapted" | raises on corrupt marker. Then:
- in `main`: if args.points and classify == adapted and not args.constrained → print error, return 2 (before any output). Actually main already checks args.ground_derived before load; add adapted-nonconstrained check.
- in `run_constrained`: adapted path.

Better: integrate into `load_input`? But `load_input` is shared by legacy main. If adapted and legacy, load_input would need to signal. Ruling says "所有入口识别manifest... 非constrained在任何写入前明确return2". So the check must be in `main` before legacy writes, and in `load_input`/`load_points` detection. Simplest: `main` calls `capture_input.classify(args.points)` first when args.points set; if adapted and not args.constrained → return 2. If adapted and constrained → run_constrained. Inside run_constrained, load adapted. Legacy load_points remains for non-adapted. And load_points/load_input could also guard: if someone calls legacy with adapted, raise. But main guard suffices + maybe defensive check in load_points. Review says "在shared input加载/主入口识别含key" — both shared input load and main entry recognize the key. So put detection in `load_points` (shared) too: if NPZ has input_manifest and it's not the adapted loader route, raise CaptureInputError (no silent legacy). But then run_constrained's adapted route must bypass load_points. Design:
  - `capture_input.is_adapted(path)` -> bool (key presence) / raises on malformed marker.
  - `load_points` (legacy): if `is_adapted(path)`: raise CaptureInputError("... use constrained adapter route ...") — so no silent legacy in shared loader.
  - `run_constrained`: before load_input, if is_adapted(args.points): use `capture_input.load_adapted`. Else legacy.
  - `main`: if args.points and is_adapted and not args.constrained → return 2 before writes. (But load_input would also raise; explicit pre-write return2 is the requirement.)

Hmm but order: main non-constrained with adapted should return 2, not crash with traceback. So explicit check in main. Good.

- M07 legacy no key: `is_adapted` false → unchanged.

Now prepare output: single NPZ, atomic exclusive link only. If os.link unavailable → reject (no O_EXCL fallback). Also calibrate artifact save_exclusive_json currently has O_EXCL fallback for platforms without link. The ruling: adapted calibration also "仅在支持atomic exclusive link时复用现save_exclusive_json（旧legacy fallback不改）". So don't modify save_exclusive_json's legacy fallback; but adapted route must refuse if link unavailable. Design: adapted route checks `getattr(os,'link',None) is not None` before proceeding; if None → return 2. And for NPZ prepare, same requirement: only link; if no link → CaptureInputError/return nonzero.

Now M11: no O_EXCL fallback retained. So update: NPZ and adapted JSON both require link; absence → explicit reject. Legacy save_exclusive_json fallback stays as-is (not changed).

Now M09 revision: "初版M09'跨pool bounds既通过又拒绝'不保留". New M09: group-first: bounds first restrict actual members, then coordinate bounds; map back pooled. So a bounds region naturally only selects its group's members. Cross-pool is not a separate case; it's handled by group-first. Good.

Now recompute group-id formula. Path-independent source content identity: use `bin_sha256` (content) + maybe meta layout hash. Let's define `source_identity = sha256(bin_sha256_hex + "|" + meta_sha256_hex)`. Then `group_id(i) = "frame:" + sha256(source_identity + "|" + str(ordinal) + "|" + str(seq) + "|" + str(stamp_sec) + "|" + str(stamp_nanosec)).hexdigest()[:24]`. Members = [[ordinal, ordinal]] (single frame: frame ordinal i, pooled rows [offset_points, offset_points+count_points)). This is deterministic, path-independent (bin content), and binds seq/stamp.

Loader rebuilds frames/group from actual source and checks manifest.frame_groups exactly equals recomputed mapping and members match actual ranges.

Now manifest schema revised:
```
{
 "schema": 1,
 "kind": "capture_input_adaptation",
 "source": {"format","format_version","tool",
            "meta_name":"meta.json","bin_name":"points.bin",
            "meta_sha256","bin_sha256","bin_size_bytes","total_points",
            "total_dropped_points":0,
            "source_bag_sha256_declared":..., "source_bag_hash_verified":false},
 "layout": {...28B...},
 "frames": [ per-frame seq/stamp/sec/nsec/bag_time/offset/count/dropped ],
 "frame_groups": { "<gid>": {"ordinal":i,"seq":..,"stamp_sec":..,"stamp_nanosec":..,
                            "rows":[offset, offset+count)} , ... },
 "points": {"key":"points","dtype":"<f4","shape":[N,3],"sha256":...},
 "declared": {"frame":<--frame>, "frame_provenance":"metadata_declared",
              "units":"m","units_provenance":"metadata_declared",
              "time_domain":...},
 "provenance": {"point_index_domain":"capture_export_row",
                "original_bag_point_index":"unknown",
                "source_bag_hash_verified":false,"physical_verified":false}
}
```

Note no paths stored (path-independent); loader takes --source-dir again and verifies against manifest. Actually if paths aren't stored, the loader can't re-read source unless it's given --source-dir. Ruling #3: "loader读实际meta/bin". So adapted CLI needs `--source-dir` too (or embedded source path?). Review #1: prepare only --source-dir. For loading, the adapted route must read actual source. Two options: (a) manifest stores source dir (path-dependent) — but review #2 says group ID path-independent, not manifest. (b) CLI `--source-dir` required for adapted load. Hmm, the acceptance says "路径不可达时明确拒绝，不从hash字符串推断已读取源；首版是本地有源输入的严格路线". So loader needs source path. Simplest and explicit: adapted load requires `--source-dir` (fixed meta.json+points.bin) alongside `--points`(NPZ). Or store source dir in manifest and require reachable. 

The 06 review #3 says loader reads actual meta/bin; doesn't forbid storing path. But #1 says prepare only supports --source-dir/--frame/--units/--output. It doesn't mention loader CLI args. The acceptance I04: "路径不可达时明确拒绝". I think embedding canonical source dir path in manifest and re-reading is the intended "local source route". But path-dependent makes group ID separate from path — fine, group id uses content.

To be safe and explicit, I'll design adapted load to require `--source-dir` (explicit), and manifest stores `source.dir` as a hint? Hmm. The acceptance says "canonical source meta/bin路径/hash". "canonical source meta/bin paths" — so manifest DOES store paths. OK: store canonical abs paths; loader re-reads them; if unreachable → reject. And group id stays path-independent (content only). That satisfies both. Good, keep paths in manifest.source.

So adapted CLI: `--points <adapted.npz>` + `--constrained` + selectors + `--output`. Loader reads manifest source paths, re-reads, verifies. If paths unreachable → reject.

Now prepare `--frame` required and must equal meta.sensor.frame_id; `--units` required and == "m". If meta has explicit units, must match; unknown type rejected.

Now let me define the actual function/order mapping for the revision, referencing file:line. Existing:
- calibrate_sensors.py: `parse_args` :157, `load_points` :96, `load_input` :204, `run_constrained` :222, `save_exclusive_json` :43, `sha256_file` :88, `load_json` :113, `load_indices` :118, `main` :337.
- ground.py: `region_indices` :504, `fit_ground_plane_constrained` :597, group checks :661-695, `validate_constrained_ground` :1031, `_normalise_indices` :479.
